narration: My shadow started walking home without me. At first, I thought it was funny. It waved from the other sidewalk. I lifted my hand. It didn't. It pointed at my yellow umbrella. I had left it beside the café. I ran back to get it. The cashier stared past my shoulder. My shadow was already at the counter. It pointed at the little clock. The hands were moving backwards again. I grabbed my umbrella and hurried outside. The sky was turning orange already. My friend laughed when I told him. Then his shadow quietly shook its head. We followed both shadows down the street. They stopped beside a locked blue door. A tiny key lay underneath the mat. My friend picked it up and hesitated. The door opened onto our classroom. Every desk was completely empty inside. Except one, right by the window. An unfinished note sat on it. It said, remember the little clock. I remembered seeing it at the café. The note had my own handwriting. I looked outside. Night had arrived. My shadow stood beneath the moon. It held out an invisible hand. I opened the umbrella over it. The streetlamp made a second shadow. That one waved at me properly. The first shadow finally smiled back. Then it pointed toward my house. I walked home with my friend. He carried the note in silence. We stopped at the front steps. The porch clock read six o'clock. Exactly when I had left earlier. The umbrella began glowing faintly yellow. I folded it and stepped inside. The hallway looked perfectly normal again. My friend knocked on the window. His shadow had disappeared completely now. I looked down at my feet. Two shadows were standing behind me. One pointed at the little clock. The other reached for the umbrella. I suddenly understood the strange warning. The clock was never running backwards. It was counting down to sunset. The umbrella kept our shadows together. I opened it before the moon. My friend's shadow returned to him. He laughed and ran back home. I put the umbrella beside my bed. The next morning everything felt normal. Until I looked at the clock. Its hands stopped exactly at six. And my umbrella was already gone.
